Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - Opens a zip, iterates its entries, and for each entry attempts to treat the current stream position as a nested zip by creating a new ZipArchiveInputStream on the same underlying stream.
  - It expects that when the nested stream points at a non-zip entry (e.g., test3.xml), reading the first entry from the nested ZipArchiveInputStream will fail with a ZipException. It records such exceptions and finally asserts there was exactly one.

- How ZipArchiveInputStream behaves:
  - ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream("zip", in) returns a ZipArchiveInputStream(in).
  - ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry() delegates to getNextZipEntry().
  - In getNextZipEntry():
    - If EOF is reached while trying to read the next local file header, it returns null (interpreted as “no more entries”).
    - It reads the first 4 bytes to determine the signature. If it sees the central directory or AES extra data signatures, it marks the central directory as hit and later returns null.
    - Critically, if the signature is not a Local File Header signature (LFH), it returns null rather than throwing an error.

- Why the test fails:
  - When attempting to read a nested archive from a non-zip entry (like test3.xml), the first 4 bytes at that position will not be an LFH signature.
  - getNextZipEntry() then returns null due to the “!LFH_SIG” branch, which is the same signal used for legitimate end-of-archive.
  - As a result, the nested read loop exits without throwing any exception, so the test doesn’t record the expected ZipException. The final assertion assertEquals(1, expectedExceptions.size()) fails.

- Relation to the bug report:
  - The report states that c0.m0() should differentiate between “invalid entry encountered” and “no more entries.” In this context, c0.m0() corresponds to ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry() (and by extension getNextEntry()).
  - The current implementation returns null on invalid signatures (i.e., not LFH), conflating “invalid data/not a zip” with “end of entries.”
  - To fix this, getNextZipEntry() should throw an exception (e.g., ZipException) when an invalid signature is encountered, while continuing to return null only for true end-of-stream/end-of-archive conditions (EOF, actual central directory termination). This change allows callers (like the test) to distinguish invalid nested archives from an exhausted archive stream.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
